disagreements.topic: FY29 EPS growth after the 70% FY28 year (the main remaining driver of fair value)
disagreements.positions: All five agents now build Sep-2027 NTM EPS from FY28 consensus $15.6 plus an FY29 they set themselves: agents 1, 2, 4, 5 at +14-15% (~$17.8-18.0), agent 3 at +10% (~$17.2), citing flat supply commitments ($87B FY28 vs $88B FY29). None of them checked the FY29 consensus.
disagreements.resolution: The sell-side consensus is much higher: FY29 EPS ~$20.1 (+29%) on revenue ~$893B (MarketScreener) and ~$20.45 (+32%, Motley Fool/YCharts). On consensus, Sep-2027 NTM EPS is ~$18.6, not ~$17.2. The agents' haircut is a defensible judgment (supply commitments disclosed today are not a ceiling on FY29, but consensus beyond a supply-constrained year is uncertain), yet it is partly offset by their 15.5-16x multiple, which is above the ~14.8x the market pays today on one-year-forward consensus ($230.73 / $15.57). Applying today's discount to consensus NTM gives ~$275 + $4 = ~$279; the agents' route gives $255-275. Reconciled ~$275, slightly above the round-2 mean of $268.
disagreements.evidence: MarketScreener NVDA estimates (FY28 EPS $15.57, FY29 $20.07; FY28 sales $683B, FY29 $893B); Motley Fool 2026-09-04 (FY28 +65%, FY29 +32% to $20.45); CFO commentary commitments table ($92B / $87B / $88B for rest of FY27 / FY28 / FY29).

disagreements.topic: Agent 3's remaining skeptic haircuts (FV $255 vs ~$270 for the others)
disagreements.positions: Agent 3: FY29 +10%, 15x NTM, 78% FCF conversion. Others: +14-15%, 15.5-17x, ~83%.
disagreements.resolution: Agent 3 took up every round-1 correction (70% guide, $51.2B stakes, 23.6B shares) and now differs only on judgment. Its conversion view (78%) is supported by the verified DSO rise to 60 days; its FY29 +10% is further below consensus (+29-32%) than anyone else. I treat the gap as legitimate dispersion, not an error, and do not remove it; it is part of why I nudge the center only ~1 pt.
disagreements.evidence: CFO commentary (AR $63.1B, DSO 60 vs 45); 10-Q payment terms 90 days to one year for investment-grade customers.

disagreements.topic: Customer concentration and credit exposure (agent 3's new quantification)
disagreements.positions: Agent 3: ACIE = $40.3B, 42% of Q2 revenue, +138% y/y; one direct customer 16% of Q2 revenue; three were 44% of H1 (via CFO commentary, Hudson Labs, Where's Your Ed At).
disagreements.resolution: Verified in primary filings: ACIE $40,313M of $96,221M (41.9%), Hyperscale $48,710M; 10-Q says one direct customer was 16% of Q2 revenue and three direct customers 16%/15%/13% of H1. Caveat: 'direct customers' include ODMs/system integrators, so these are not end-customer credit exposures; the AI-cloud credit risk sits in ACIE. The facts support a fat left tail but add nothing new to the base case.
disagreements.evidence: 8-K Ex-99.2 CFO commentary revenue-by-market table; 10-Q Note 7 and MD&A concentration language.

disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 2, 4: $160; agent 3: $158; agent 5: $155, arguing $160 sits within a normal 28% shock drawdown (~$166) plus noise and would trigger without a fundamental break.
disagreements.resolution: Agent 5's point is fair: $160 is only ~$6 below an average shock-drawdown level. I move to $158 (~10.1x FY28 consensus, ~8.5x consensus NTM at the horizon, below the $164.27 52-week low). This is the round-2 mean in effect.

one_month_reasoning: No NVIDIA earnings before Oct 30 (Q3 call Nov 17); the window holds TSMC Q3 (mid-Oct), GTC Berlin (Oct 21), the late-October hyperscaler capex prints and a live Oct 28 FOMC (~35% hike odds after the soft Sep 30 PCE), with Micron's Sep 30 after-close beat a mild positive; all five agents now agree on these, so I keep their mean: a near-symmetric ~11% monthly spread centred just above spot with a slightly fat lower tail.
confidence_reason: Round-2 forecasts converged (FV $255-275, P(>=spot) 0.585-0.613) once the round-1 facts were taken up. My one new finding, that the FY29 consensus is ~+30% (EPS ~$20.1) while every agent assumed +10-15%, points up, but it is partly offset by the multiples the agents chose and consensus two years out is soft, so I nudge the center only ~1 pt (K=231-346) and leave the tails and 1-month ladder at the mean.
thesis_break_reason: $158 is ~32% below spot, below the $164.27 52-week low and past NVDA's average ~28% shock drawdown (~$166), and ~10x FY28 consensus EPS ($15.6) or ~8.5x consensus NTM EPS at the horizon. A close there would mean the market has stopped believing the supply-constrained ~70% FY28 outlook (Vera Rubin cuts or pushouts, hyperscaler capex cuts) or that credit stress in the AI-cloud book (ACIE, 42% of revenue) is hitting the $63B receivables, $279B commitments or $94B of stakes.
key_drivers: Management guides ~70% FY28 revenue growth, supply-constrained, at 72-73% GM; FY28 consensus EPS ~$15.6 is consistent with a bottom-up ~$15.9.

FY29 is the swing: consensus is ~$20.1 EPS (+29%, revenue ~$893B) while the forecasters assume +10-15%; NTM EPS at Sep 2027 is ~$17.2-18.6 depending on which is right, and the multiple on it (market pays ~14.8x one-year-forward consensus today) decides the outcome.
Cash conversion is weakening (Q2 OCF $24.1B vs NI $59.7B, DSO 45 -> 60 days on extended terms), so FY28 FCF is ~$300-320B rather than ~0.9x NI.

Balance-sheet-funded demand is the left tail: $279B supply commitments, $108.5B guarantees (the $105B piece starts in FY29), $36B AI-cloud agreements, $94B of stakes, and ACIE (neoclouds, AI natives, sovereign) now 42% of revenue.
The $235B buyback through FY28 retires ~3% of shares by Sep 2027 (~23.6B diluted) and adds ~$4/sh of net cash and haircut stakes.

fair_value.reason: Two routes. Agents' route: NTM EPS at Sep 2027 ~$17.2 (FY28 $15.6, FY29 +14%) x 16x = $275, + ~$4/sh net cash and haircut stakes = ~$279, or $255-275 across the five agents. Consensus route: NTM ~$18.6 (1/3 x $15.57 + 2/3 x $20.07) x the ~14.8x the market pays today for one-year-forward consensus = $275, + $4 = $279. FCF cross-check: ~$315B FY28 FCF at 5% / 23.6B shares + $4 = ~$271. Reconciled ~$275, above the round-2 mean of $268.4 because the agents' FY29 growth sits well below consensus.

summary: Round 2 converged: all five forecasters took up the round-1 corrections (70% FY28 guide, 72-73% GM, $235B buyback, ~$117B net cash and stakes, weaker cash conversion), and fair values now sit at $255-275 (mean $268) with P(close >= $231) ~0.59. The one new fact is that the FY29 consensus (~$20.1 EPS, +29%) is far above every agent's +10-15%, which lifts the reconciled fair value to ~$275, but I nudge the ladder up only ~1 pt because the agents' multiples partly offset it and consensus beyond a supply-constrained year is soft. The left tail stays fat: DSO at 60 days, $279B of commitments, and AI-cloud customers (42% of revenue) whose funding depends on credit markets. Thesis break $158; no in-window earnings, but a live Oct 28 FOMC.
